name: sodapy-tutorial-nyc-opendata
what_it_holds: MIT-licensed, three-notebook tutorial (API basics, SoQL query language, sample 311-data analysis) for pulling any Socrata-backed open-data portal via the sodapy Python client; 45 commits; not STR-specific but the exact mechanism needed for Nashville, Seattle, Denver, Chicago, Boston (Analyze Boston) and San Diego open-data portals, all of which run Socrata.
why_useful: Lower-friction Python alternative to the R nycOpenData package for the same NYC OSE registration pull; marginal beyond that package.
duplicate_of_holding: same purpose as ropensci/nycOpenData candidate above
themes: Inside Airbnb New York City snapshots around Local Law 18 (2023-06 to 2024-03) stored in repos

Municipal short-term-rental licence and registration datasets (Austin, LA HSO, SF OSTR, Denver, New Orleans, Nashville, Seattle, Portland, Boston, Chicago, San Diego, Honolulu) mirrored or pulled by code
Open-data portal discovery: Socrata/CKAN/data.gov/EU data portal clients, dataset search tools, Google Dataset Search scrapers; city portals with STR datasets
why_all: Lower-friction Python alternative to the R nycOpenData package for the same NYC OSE registration pull; marginal beyond that package.

Directly serves gap #17 (Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery clients to find STR datasets across cities) — a clean, documented starting point for writing one reusable puller against the Socrata SODA API that could hit Nashville/Seattle/Denver/Chicago/Boston/San Diego STR endpoints identified in this same search.

Concrete example of hitting the exact portal (data.cityofnewyork.us) that hosts NYC's STR registration dataset; could help re-pull or verify the NYC OSE registry the team already has, or locate a longer-history NYC STR dataset ID via the same client.

name: CityOfLosAngeles/short-term-rental-spec
what_it_holds: Official City of Los Angeles GitHub org repo containing the Platform Sharing API specification (platform-sharing/v1.0.yaml, also on SwaggerHub) that STR platforms use to report listing compliance data to LA under the Home-Sharing Ordinance; Apache-2.0 licensed, 39 commits, actively maintained by the city itself.
why_useful: It is the authoritative schema for what LA's STR compliance API returns (registration status per listing), which is the blueprint needed to build any future point-in-time LA HSO puller; also documents the compliance-reporting field structure other cities model.
themes: Municipal short-term-rental licence and registration datasets (Austin, LA HSO, SF OSTR, Denver, New Orleans, Nashville, Seattle, Portland, Boston, Chicago, San Diego, Honolulu) mirrored or pulled by code
why_all: It is the authoritative schema for what LA's STR compliance API returns (registration status per listing), which is the blueprint needed to build any future point-in-time LA HSO puller; also documents the compliance-reporting field structure other cities model.

Not a dataset, but the authoritative schema for what compliance/registration fields LA (and any city adopting the same open spec) actually captures on STR platforms — useful for understanding what a scraped or FOIA'd LA HSO extract would contain, and it is a government-maintained repo (credible, low-risk source) rather than a third party's guess.

name: TOHS-tool-rbc (Rental Background Check)
what_it_holds: Daily GitHub-Actions pipeline normalizing Toronto Short-Term Rental Registry data plus Ontario Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB) order catalogue, Toronto RentSafeTO, active building permits, multi-tenant house licences and planned developments into address-keyed JSON files (data/a.json ... data/z.json, data/0-9.json); 392 commits, code MIT-licensed, published data dual-licensed under Open Government Licence Toronto/Ontario.
why_useful: Broader than the Toronto STR-only mirror above — bundles STR registration with landlord/tenant enforcement and building-permit data for the same city, useful for cross-referencing registration compliance with housing-supply signals; also a working template for building a similar address-keyed daily STR+housing pipeline for a US city.
size_hint: 27 partitioned JSON files, address-keyed, size unconfirmed
license: code MIT; data under Open Government Licence – Toronto / Ontario
duplicate_of_holding: partially overlaps candidate above for the STR slice; adds LTB/permits not in our holdings
themes: Municipal short-term-rental licence and registration datasets (Austin, LA HSO, SF OSTR, Denver, New Orleans, Nashville, Seattle, Portland, Boston, Chicago, San Diego, Honolulu) mirrored or pulled by code
Canadian and Australian STR registries and datasets (Toronto, Vancouver, Montreal, Quebec CITQ, BC registry, Sydney NSW STRA register, Melbourne)
why_all: Broader than the Toronto STR-only mirror above — bundles STR registration with landlord/tenant enforcement and building-permit data for the same city, useful for cross-referencing registration compliance with housing-supply signals; also a working template for building a similar address-keyed daily STR+housing pipeline for a US city.

A second, independently-built daily mirror of Toronto's STR registry (cross-check/backup for the RamVasuthevan repo above) plus adjacent housing-supply signals (building permits, multi-tenant licences) that bear on long-term vs short-term rental crossover economics for a major Canadian ABNB market (gap #12 and #13).

name: robbins
what_it_holds: Streamlit app + DuckDB/dbt warehouse for Seattle-metro public data; explicitly ingests Seattle's Short-Term Rental License dataset (Socrata id s7df-xba4, ~8,100 records per the city portal) alongside other Socrata SODA API, ArcGIS FeatureServer and federal-bulk-file sources; author states the pipeline is 'replicable across cities through configuration changes only'.
why_useful: A working, documented one-command pull for Seattle STR licenses (one of the named theme cities) plus a config-driven pattern that could be repointed at Denver/Nashville/Chicago/SF Socrata STR endpoints with minimal work — directly useful as acquisition-method tooling for gap #12 and #17 (Socrata discovery/client tooling).
time_coverage: current snapshot via live Socrata pull, not a historical archive
size_hint: ~8,100 Seattle STR license records (per city portal, not committed to repo)
duplicate_of_holding: Seattle not in our current 25-dataset municipal STR list

name: diagmatrix/tourism-watcher
what_it_holds: Python monitoring project for Granada, Spain that (a) scrapes Airbnb search results directly for 'Granada, España' with flexible dates, and (b) has an in-progress secondary track pulling public tourist-housing permit data. Data collection in a `data/` folder starting 2024-10-15; 18 commits; GPL-3.0. Per the README the permit/registry side (the useful, non-Airbnb half for our purposes) is still described as under development, not yet delivering committed registry data.
why_useful: The permit-registry half, if completed, would be another Spanish-city STR licence dataset (gap 12); flagged mainly because the primary/working half of the tool scrapes Airbnb search pages directly, which is out of scope under our sanctioned-sources rule -- catalogue only, do not run.
size_hint: Small, early-stage; data folder exists but registry portion incomplete
duplicate_of_holding: Partially overlaps existing Inside Airbnb Barcelona coverage in spirit but different city (Granada) and different source (permit registry, once built)
themes: European STR registration and tourist-accommodation registries (Portugal RNAL, Spain tourist dwellings, Italy CIN, France meublés de tourisme, Amsterdam, Berlin, Vienna, Lisbon, Barcelona HUTB, Paris)
why_all: The permit-registry half, if completed, would be another Spanish-city STR licence dataset (gap 12); flagged mainly because the primary/working half of the tool scrapes Airbnb search pages directly, which is out of scope under our sanctioned-sources rule -- catalogue only, do not run.

Combines a public STR registry pull with an Airbnb listing scrape for one Spanish city — a method template for cross-checking registration counts against live listing counts (relevant to the RNPL/registration-coverage question), though it does touch airbnb.com and any run decision is a human call per repo rules.
